summary: Small, well-factored module (142 lines). The make_vector factory, deleted-ctor guard, StructRefProxy properties and the three operator overloads are idiomatic and free of dead code, hidden config, or stale comments. The only DES observation is a minor duplication of the grow-and-copy reallocation block between vector_push and vector_extend; both are local and low-impact.

findings.title: Reallocation grow-and-copy block duplicated between vector_push and vector_extend
findings.claim: The three-line 'allocate a new buffer, copy the live prefix, swap it in' idiom is copy-pasted in vector_push (lines 123-125) and vector_extend (lines 137-139). A future change to the growth/copy strategy (e.g. switching to numpy.resize, copying via a typed view, or adjusting the growth factor) must be made in two places and can drift between push and extend. This is a maintenance hazard, not a runtime defect.
findings.evidence: vector_push: `new_buf = numpy.empty(v.buf.shape[0] * 2, v.buf.dtype)` / `new_buf[:v.size] = v.buf[:v.size]` / `v.buf = new_buf` (lines 123-125). vector_extend repeats the same shape: `new_buf = numpy.empty(cap, dst.buf.dtype)` / `new_buf[:dst.size] = dst.buf[:dst.size]` / `dst.buf = new_buf` (lines 137-139). The only real difference is how the new capacity is computed (single double vs. `while cap < needed: cap *= 2`).
findings.recommendation: Optional, low-risk: extract an `@njit(**jit_options)` helper `_grow_to(v, new_cap)` that allocates `numpy.empty(new_cap, v.buf.dtype)`, copies `[:v.size]`, and assigns `v.buf`, then call it from both. Keep the distinct capacity calculations (push needs exactly one doubling since it only ever adds one slot; extend must loop to reach `needed`) at the call sites. Given the repo's surgical-change bias and that this is two short call sites, leaving it as-is is also defensible.
